subject: HelioPay onboarding — p50/p95 measurement carveout proposal
messages:
From: Samuel Lee <samuel@heliopay.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@heliopay.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency commitment question for HelioPay go-live

Hi Olga,

Quick note from the HelioPay eng team as we lock down go-live next week. Our payment auth traffic has a very sharp diurnal pattern — heavy bursts between 09:00–11:30 and 17:30–19:00 PT. For the hosted API we want firm p50/p95 commitments in the contract, but we also need flexibility during the first 72 hours of production while our autoscaling configs and rate-limiting rules settle.

Current ask: can Redwood provide the standard p50/p95 targets for our plan and — as a one-time concession for onboarding — allow a temporary p95 measurement window relaxation or a daypart carveout for the two peak windows to avoid false SLA breaches? If so, what would that look like (numbers & duration)? Also need the monitoring hooks so our SREs can see the rollforward.

Thanks,
Sam
Samuel Lee
Head of Platform
HelioPay

Subject: RE: Latency commitment question for HelioPay go-live

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the go-live window. We can do a limited, documented exception during onboarding; below is a practical proposal that balances customer risk with our production guarantees.

Proposal (temporary onboarding carveout) — summary:
- Standard commitments (post-onboarding): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 450ms measured on a rolling 1-hour window aggregated across the hosted API endpoint group you use.
- Temporary carveout: for the first 72 hours after your production cutover we propose a daypart carveout for the two peak windows (09:00–11:30 PT, 17:30–19:00 PT). During those windows we will use a relaxed p95 target of 700ms, measured on a rolling 3-hour window, for the purposes of SLA assessment only. Outside the dayparts we keep the standard 1-hour window & targets.
- Conditions: carveout applies once, begins at the timestamp of confirmed cutover, and automatically expires after 72 hours. Redwood will not apply credits for performance within the carveout window but will provide incident-grade visibility and a joint post-mortem if p95 exceeds 1s prolonged.
- Mitigations we will enable immediately: autoscale threshold lower to 60% CPU/GPU utilization for your dedicated pool (hosted-tier burst), prefix-based KV caching for repeated auth flows, and a fallback model variant (quantized) for non-critical paths to reduce tail latency.

Attached I’m including an analysis of your sample traffic (heliopay_p95_analysis.csv) and a draft temporary SLO amendment PDF. Operational next steps we need from HelioPay:
1) Confirm cutover time window (start timestamp).
2) Share on-call channel for SRE (Slack/ops pager).
3) Approve the SLO amendment PDF or suggest redlines.

CCing Marissa for commercial/credits language and Lauren for measurement/observability follow-up. If that all looks reasonable we’ll prepare an update to the contract plus a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to run the steps.

Best,
Olga Petrov

Olga — good approach. A couple commercial notes:
- We should offer a one-time credit cadence if HelioPay hits repeated SLA misses outside the carveout (suggest 25% service credit of monthly hosted usage for measurable p95 breach >72 hours after cutover).
- Legal/procurement will want language that the carveout is time-limited and non-precedential.

Sam — if you’re good with the 72-hour carveout & the relaxed 700ms p95 during the two dayparts, we’ll queue Legal to produce the final amendment and procurement to prep DocuSign. Can you confirm whether you want the credit fallback clause included in the amendment?

—Marissa

Thanks Olga & Marissa — that proposal looks reasonable and pragmatic. A few quick clarifications from our side:
1) Monitoring: can Redwood add a read-only dashboard link for our SREs (Prometheus/Grafana-style) and a webhook to push p95 alerts to our ops Slack channel?

3) Credits: yes, please include the credit fallback clause in the amendment; we’ll consider it a safety valve.

If you send the DocuSign I’ll route to procurement & legal on our side and confirm the cutover start time (targeting 2027-06-01T16:00:00-07:00 PT).

Sam
